facts.label: Analytical read-through
facts.text: - Usable coverage: seven dated filings span the FY2025 audited year and each 2026 quarter. Together they support a reported financial foundation, a last-twelve-months view from the Q3 release's discrete quarters, and a debt and liquidity description of a capital structure that has one note series and one undrawn revolver. - Strongest contrary evidence: the pending Business Combination (10-Q Q3 page:11 to page:12) can change ownership, covenant treatment and the debt structure. The 10-K (page:127) says that on a "Change of Control Triggering Event" the issuers "may be required to make an offer to repurchase" the notes at "101.0%" of principal. The supplied set does not say whether that event is triggered by the Transocean transaction. It also does not give the combination financing, Transocean's capital structure or the post-closing group. - Source risk mechanism: the revolver's "financial covenants that require us to maintain (i) a minimum book value of equity to total assets ratio, (ii) a minimum interest coverage ratio and (iii) a minimum amount of liquidity" (10-K page:129) carry no printed level, so a consumer cannot compute headroom and must not infer a pass from the statement that the company is "in compliance in all material respects". Compliance is a management assertion in a filing, not a tested ratio. - Second mechanism: ARO is outside consolidated debt and earnings. Valaris reports notes receivable from ARO, an investment, lease receivables and payables, a contingent funding commitment for newbuild jackups, and ARO's own revolver and term loan (10-Q Q3 page:54 to page:56). A consumer that reads only consolidated debt omits an exposure that can call on Valaris cash. ARO's statements are not supplied, so the exposure can be described from Valaris's disclosure only. - Third mechanism: letters of credit and surety bonds sit outside the revolver. The Q3 10-Q (page:26) says none "were issued under the 2028 Credit Agreement". Revolver availability therefore must not be reduced for them without evidence, and must not be assumed unaffected by other conditions on borrowing. - What cannot proceed: covenant headroom against levels, rating-based pricing, post-closing credit analysis of the combined group, legal interpretation of the indenture and credit agreement, guarantor-level analysis, ARO standalone credit analysis. - Next evidence action: supply the Business Combination Agreement and any scheme document or proxy, the Indenture dated April 19, 2023 and the 2028 Credit Agreement with covenant definitions, any ratings reports, ARO's financial statements, and any filing dated between November 3, 2026 and the cutoff.

rows.label: The seven filings are enough for a financial base view, a business and transaction view, a credit synthesis and an evidence trace, each with stated limits. The pending Transocean combination is the central transaction.
Audited FY2025 statements and three 2026 interim filings with matching earnings releases are located, with quarterly columns through Q3 2026.
Debt is one 8.375% second lien note series due 2030 plus an undrawn $375.0 million revolver maturing 2028.
The revolver has three financial covenants, but no test level or reported figure is printed.
The pending Transocean combination changes ownership; the notes carry change-of-control terms, and whether the combination triggers them is not stated.
ARO is an unconsolidated 50/50 joint venture with notes receivable and possible capital calls; only summary disclosure is supplied.
Financial covenant levels and reported covenant figures not supplied (three tests named only)
Business Combination Agreement, scheme document, proxy and combination financing not supplied; effect on the notes and revolver not stated
Executed Indenture and 2028 Credit Agreement, guarantor list and collateral schedules not supplied
Events from November 3, 2026 to the cutoff not supplied
ARO standalone financial statements not supplied; only Valaris's disclosure
No ratings, market prices or peer data (context fields empty)

Adjusted EBITDA and backlog are management measures that appear only in the releases; the 10-Qs and the 10-K print no Adjusted EBITDA, and the release gives a definition and segment rows but no line-by-line bridge from net income
Reclassified prior-period amounts (Q3 10-Q page:11) may differ from the 10-K
Text extraction only; charts, images and original table layout not inspected

The recomputation from reported lines reproduces the issuer figures for Q3 2026 (150.6), nine months 2026 (313.8) and FY2025 (642.2); see Calculations. The statement runs from page:105 (revenues to depreciation) to page:106 (general and administrative to net income). No figure in CP-0 is affected. - Prior-period comparability: the 2026 10-Qs state that certain previous amounts were reclassified. No difference between FY2025 totals in the 10-K and the Q4 2025 column plus nine-month 2025 figures was found: FY2025 operating cash flow of 546.2 equals nine months 2025 of 474.0 plus Q4 2025 of 72.2, and capital expenditure of 343.5 equals 237.2 plus 106.3. - Net income quality: FY2025 net income of 979.1 includes a total income tax benefit of 426.8, of which a deferred benefit of 515.1 (10-K page:106), tied to reductions in valuation allowances on deferred tax assets (10-K page:142). Q4 2025 net income of 716.8 carries a benefit of 680.4 (Q3 release page:8). Earnings-based ratios should use Adjusted EBITDA or operating income, not net income.

Liquidity is cash plus the undrawn $375.0 million revolver, 900.1 at September 30, 2026; no debt principal falls due before 2030.
The revolver carries three financial covenants but no level or reported figure is printed.
The pending Transocean combination and ARO funding commitments sit outside the reported debt figure.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The central transaction is the pending acquisition of Valaris by Transocean Ltd. under a Business Combination Agreement dated February 9, 2026. It is a share exchange at 15.235 Transocean shares for each Valaris share, implemented by a Bermuda court-approved scheme of arrangement, and no cash consideration is described. Valaris shareholders would own about 47% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis assuming conversion of Transocean's exchangeable bonds due 2029. Shareholder meetings are set for November 24, 2026, a court hearing for November 26, 2026, and closing is expected on or about December 1, 2026. These are expectations, not completed events. For a creditor the important point is what the sources do not say: no supplied document states whether the combination triggers the change-of-control offer in the Indenture, whether the notes or revolver stay in place, or what the combined capital structure is. Until closing, the agreement restricts dividends, share repurchases, asset encumbrance, acquisitions and dispositions, and new or guaranteed debt.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The one transaction in the sources is the pending business combination with Transocean Ltd., a Swiss corporation. The Business Combination Agreement was entered into on February 9, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:11). Transocean will acquire all issued and outstanding common shares of Valaris in exchange for Transocean shares at an exchange ratio of 15.235 Transocean shares for each Valaris share, by a court-approved scheme of arrangement under section 99 of the Companies Act 1981 of Bermuda (10-K page:8). Outstanding warrants will be assumed by Transocean and remain exercisable for the Fundamental Transaction Consideration as defined in the Warrant Agreement dated April 30, 2021 (10-Q Q3 page:11). On a fully diluted basis assuming conversion of Transocean's exchangeable bonds due 2029, Transocean shareholders would own approximately 53% and Valaris shareholders 47% of the combined company (10-Q Q3 page:11). The type is a stock-for-stock acquisition of Valaris. There is no sponsor, no cash consideration and no use of proceeds in the sources.

facts.text: Terms that matter to creditors. A termination fee of $173.0 million is payable by Valaris in specified circumstances; if Valaris shareholders fail to approve and that fee is not otherwise payable, Valaris must reimburse Transocean's transaction expenses up to $58 million (10-K page:22). Either party may terminate if the effective time has not occurred by February 9, 2027, subject to extension (10-K page:22). Valaris is restricted from soliciting alternative proposals and cannot terminate to accept a superior proposal (10-K page:23). Interim covenants restrict amending organizational documents, declaring dividends or repurchasing shares, encumbering assets, acquisitions and dispositions, incurring or guaranteeing indebtedness, and entering or amending material contracts (10-K page:24). Merger and integration expenses were 15.5 in Q3 2026 and 40.5 for nine months 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:12), per the financial base view.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: - Revenue durability. Evidence: backlog of 4,750.1 at November 2, 2026 against 4,672.3 at February 17, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:35), with contracts that may be terminated for convenience or lack of FID (10-K page:10). Mechanic: contracted day rates give revenue visibility for debt service, but termination rights and the FID contingency make part of the backlog conditional. Implication: contracted revenue supports near-term liquidity while the notes do not mature before 2030; the conditionality argues against treating backlog as committed cash. Counter-evidence: none logged; the backlog by year at November 2, 2026 is Not supplied. - Margin and cash flow risk. Evidence: drillship average daily revenue rose to $469,000 in Q3 2026 while floater utilization was 58% (Q3 release page:12), and capital expenditure above operating cash flow in 2026 per the financial base view. Mechanic: idle or stacked rigs carry fixed cost, and contract-specific upgrades precede revenue. Implication: improving drillship contracting should lift cash flow, but liquidity depends on those rigs starting work on schedule. - Concentration. Evidence: five customers at 49% of FY2025 revenues and 11 rigs on national oil company contracts (10-K page:11, page:45). Mechanic: loss or renegotiation of one contract is material, and national oil company terms can be non-negotiable. Implication: tail risk on any single contract; no customer credit assessment is supplied. - Transaction and creditor control. Evidence: the stock-for-stock combination, the Indenture's change-of-control offer at 101.0%, and the silence of the sources on debt treatment. Mechanic: closing could trigger noteholder rights or change covenant tests, and interim covenants limit new debt until closing. Implication: standalone credit metrics may not describe the issuer after December 1, 2026. This is the key uncertainty. - ARO. Evidence: notes receivable, newbuild funding commitment, and ARO's thin cash against rising newbuild orders (10-Q Q3 page:54 to page:56). Mechanic: an unconsolidated affiliate can draw on Valaris cash without appearing in debt. Implication: contingent liquidity use; the commitment is a maximum, not an expected call. - Sponsor alignment. Evidence: no sponsor, no dividends, no repurchases in 2026. Mechanic: no extraction channel is documented. Implication: neutral; behaviour after closing is Not supplied.

rows.label: Valaris is an offshore driller whose standalone credit picture is overtaken by a pending share-for-share sale to Transocean, expected to close on or about December 1, 2026. Backlog is 4,750.1 and ARO adds off-balance-sheet exposure.
Transocean will acquire all Valaris shares at 15.235 Transocean shares each by court-approved scheme, with shareholder meetings on November 24, 2026.
Revenue rests on day rate contracts; backlog was 4,750.1 on November 2, 2026, and the largest customers are Petrobras, BP and Azule.
ARO, a 50/50 joint venture with Saudi Aramco, owes Valaris notes receivable and may call on Valaris for newbuild funding.
Valaris has paid no dividends and made no share repurchases in 2026, and the combination agreement restricts both and new debt.
The Middle East conflict reduced operating income and added insurance cost in 2026.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Valaris Ltd has a low standalone refinancing risk and moderate leverage, but its credit quality now depends on a takeover whose effect on creditors is not disclosed. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 900.1 million and no debt principal due before 2030. The weakest point is cash generation: over the last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA of USD 410.8 million was below capital expenditure of USD 434.3 million, and cash fell. Three things decide the outcome: whether idle drillships keep returning to work at higher day rates, how the combination treats the USD 1,100.0 million of notes, and whether ARO draws on Valaris cash. Confidence is Medium.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Liquidity is the anchor. Valaris held cash of USD 525.1 million and an undrawn USD 375.0 million revolver at September 30, 2026, giving liquidity of USD 900.1 million. The only debt is USD 1,100.0 million of 8.375% second lien notes due April 30, 2030, and the revolver matures April 3, 2028 with nothing drawn. The notes' fair value of USD 1,125.2 million exceeded their principal, which does not point to market stress. - Earnings fell and then turned. Adjusted EBITDA, the company's own measure, was USD 642.2 million in FY2025 and USD 410.8 million over the last twelve months to Q3 2026, but USD 150.6 million in Q3 2026 against USD 96.5 million in Q2 2026. Gross leverage on principal moved from 1.71x to 2.68x and net leverage from 0.78x to 1.40x. The latest quarter is the strongest of the last four, so the last-twelve-months ratios overstate the current run rate, though the sources give no forecast. - Spending outruns cash flow. Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of USD 155.3 million did not cover capital expenditure of USD 328.0 million, and the 2026 capital expenditure guidance is USD 445.0 million to USD 470.0 million. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD -206.8 million over the last twelve months. The guidance describes maintenance and upgrade projects including contract-specific work, so part of the spending should earn revenue as rigs start work, but it is funded from cash until then. - The takeover is the main unknown. Transocean Ltd. will acquire Valaris by share exchange, with closing expected on or about December 1, 2026. The sources do not state whether closing triggers the notes' change-of-control repurchase offer at 101.0%, whether the notes and revolver stay in place, or what the combined capital structure is. Until closing, the agreement restricts new debt, dividends and repurchases. - Covenant headroom cannot be judged. The revolver carries minimum equity to total assets, minimum interest coverage and minimum liquidity tests with no printed level or reported figure. The company states only that it was in compliance in all material respects. - ARO is an off-balance-sheet claim on liquidity. Valaris holds notes receivable from ARO with a carrying value of USD 363.4 million that mature in 2027 and 2028 and are subordinated, and it may have to fund ARO newbuilds up to about USD 1.1 billion. ARO had cash of USD 32.1 million and has never paid a distribution. - Contracted revenue gives visibility but not certainty. Backlog was USD 4,750.1 million at November 2, 2026, concentrated in a few customers, and contracts can be terminated for convenience or if a customer fails to reach a final investment decision.

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: 1. Q4 2026 cash outlay before operating inflows (indicative, not a forecast). Remaining 2026 capital expenditure from guidance: 445.0 - 328.0 = 117.0 and 470.0 - 328.0 = 142.0. Scheduled October 30, 2026 coupon: 1,100.0 x 8.375% / 2 = 46.1 (from the financial base view). Outlay = 117.0 + 46.1 = 163.1 to 142.0 + 46.1 = 188.1. Cash after these outlays and with no operating cash flow, asset sale proceeds or merger costs: 525.1 - 163.1 = 362.0 to 525.1 - 188.1 = 337.0. Adding the undrawn revolver: 362.0 + 375.0 = 737.0 to 337.0 + 375.0 = 712.0. Q3 2026 operating cash flow was 67.2, which is excluded here. Whether the coupon was paid is not stated in the sources. 2. Adjusted EBITDA less capital expenditure: last twelve months to Q3 2026, 410.8 - 434.3 = -23.5; nine months 2026, 313.8 - 328.0 = -14.2; FY2025, 642.2 - 343.5 = 298.7. Inputs are from the financial base view. 3. Notes fair value over principal at September 30, 2026: 1,125.2 - 1,100.0 = 25.1; 1,125.2 / 1,100.0 = 102.3% of principal. Quoted prices are Level 1 inputs per the filing. The redemption price schedule is 104.188% until April 30, 2027 and 102.094% from then until April 30, 2028 (financial base view). 4. ## Request

- Execution: host session. The analyst read the pinned files and wrote this answer. No provider was called.
- Question: can the supplied public filings support the four consumers, and what remains blocked?

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven filings are enough for a financial base view, a business and transaction view, a credit synthesis and an evidence trace, each with stated limits. The pending Transocean combination is the central transaction. | Medium | Covenant levels, ratings, executed debt documents, the combination agreement and ARO's own statements are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Audited FY2025 statements and three 2026 interim filings with matching earnings releases are located, with quarterly columns through Q3 2026. | Supports a last-twelve-months and quarterly credit view on a consolidated basis. | High |

| Debt is one 8.375% second lien note series due 2030 plus an undrawn $375.0 million revolver maturing 2028. | Debt terms are limited to two instruments, but guarantor and collateral detail rests on filing summaries only. | Medium |
| The revolver has three financial covenants, but no test level or reported figure is printed. | Covenant headroom cannot be assessed from these sources. | High |

| The pending Transocean combination changes ownership; the notes carry change-of-control terms, and whether the combination triggers them is not stated. | Post-closing credit profile and note treatment are not supplied; analysis stays standalone. | Medium |

| ARO is an unconsolidated 50/50 joint venture with notes receivable and possible capital calls; only summary disclosure is supplied. | ARO exposure can be sized from Valaris's disclosure but not tested against ARO's own accounts. | Medium |
### Readiness view

All four selected consumers are READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS. None is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED, because each owner can perform its method on located, dated filings. The limitations are bounded gaps, not missing identity or period evidence. The perimeter is consolidated Valaris Limited and subsidiaries, with ARO accounted for under the equity method. The latest evidence is the Q3 2026 earnings release (November 2, 2026) and the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q (signed November 3, 2026), both before the cutoff. Nothing dated after the cutoff is supplied or used. Readiness here covers source sufficiency only; it does not say the downstream analysis is complete.
| Consumer | Status | Basis |

| CP-1 (financial base view) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | FY2025 audited statements (10-K page:105 to page:107) and Q3 2026 condensed statements (10-Q Q3 page:8 to page:10) are located. The Q3 release gives five discrete quarters (page:8 to page:11). Segment, backlog, utilization and debt text are located. Facility-level carrying values for the revolver are not needed: no amount is outstanding. Text extraction flattens tables. |

| CP-1A (business and transaction) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business, segments, customers, the Transocean Business Combination Agreement, ARO and fleet actions are located (10-K page:8, page:76, page:155; 10-Q Q3 page:11, page:12, page:32). The agreement itself, a proxy or scheme document and later 8-Ks are not supplied. |

| CP-2 (credit synthesis) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Liquidity, debt, maturity, commitments and the covenant categories are located (10-Q Q3 page:51 to page:56; 10-K page:127 to page:129). Covenant levels, ratings and market prices are not supplied. |
| CP-5 (evidence trace) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Every source has stable page chunks, so claims can be traced. The original HTML, charts and images are not inspected. |
Command sheet: CP-1 RUN; CP-1A RUN; CP-2 RUN; CP-5 RUN.
### Source register

- Family and authority: filed annual report, original authority for audited consolidated statements. page:1: "FORM 10-K", "For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025", "Commission File Number 1-8097", "Valaris Limited". Signed February 20, 2026 (page:163). The Q3 10-Q (page:11) confirms the 10-K was "filed with the SEC on February 20, 2026".
- Audit: KPMG LLP (page:102, page:104, page:105); page:104 contains "served as the Company's auditor since".

- Statements located: balance sheet page:106, statements of operations page:105, cash flows page:107. Debt note from page:127 (2030 Second Lien Notes), page:128 (indenture covenants, 2028 Credit Agreement security), page:129 (revolver pricing, financial covenants). Fair values page:124. Contractual obligations page:91. Letters of credit page:93. Backlog page:76. ARO notes page:121 to page:124.
- Units: USD millions unless stated. Perimeter: consolidated Valaris Limited and subsidiaries; ARO is a variable interest entity that Valaris does not consolidate (page:122).
#### Forms 10-Q for Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026

- Q1 (`10-Q_2026-03-31_val-20260331.htm.jsonl`): "For the quarterly period ended March 31, 2026"; signed May 5, 2026 (page:53). Unaudited condensed statements (balance sheet page:9). Debt and revolver text page:19 to page:20.
- Q2 (`10-Q_2026-06-30_val-20260630.htm.jsonl`): "For the quarterly period ended June 30, 2026"; signed August 6, 2026 (page:57). Letters of credit text page:24 and page:51.

- Q3 (`10-Q_2026-09-30_val-20260930.htm.jsonl`): "For the quarterly period ended September 30, 2026"; signed November 3, 2026 (page:62). Statements page:8 to page:10; business combination page:11 to page:12 and page:32; debt page:21 to page:22; contingencies page:26; supplemental balances page:29 to page:30; liquidity page:51 to page:56. "As of October 29, 2026, there were 69,443,058 Common Shares of the registrant outstanding" (page:1).

- Authority: filed, unaudited, controlling for statement facts of their periods. The Q3 10-Q shows a three-month and nine-month column for 2026 and 2025, so quarter and year-to-date figures can be kept apart.

- Version relationship: the Q3 10-Q (page:11) says certain previously reported amounts "have been reclassified to conform to the current year presentation". Where the FY2025 comparatives differ from the 10-K, the 10-K remains the original audited source and the difference must be logged downstream, not smoothed.
#### Earnings releases (Exhibit 99.1)

- Authority: management-prepared, unaudited. They carry reported statements, segment Adjusted EBITDA (Q3 release page:10 to page:11, with the definition of Adjusted EBITDA in its footnote), backlog (page:11), average daily revenue, utilization and management narrative. Management narrative and backlog are attributed management claims, not audited facts.

- Version relationship: the Q3 release repeats statement figures that also appear in the Q3 10-Q (for example revenues, net income, cash and cash equivalents). Treat the 10-Q as controlling for statement facts and do not count the release as independent corroboration. The release alone supplies Adjusted EBITDA, backlog and five-quarter trends.

- The Q3 release (page:5) states that Valaris "does not intend to hold future earnings conference calls or provide updates to forward-looking guidance". No current guidance is therefore available beyond the capital expenditure range in the 10-Q (page:52).
### Information-availability boundary
- Every issuer document is dated on or before November 3, 2026, before the cutoff of 2026-11-05.

- Forward dates in the Q3 10-Q (shareholder meetings on November 24, 2026, court hearing on November 26, 2026, expected closing on or about December 1, 2026; page:12) are labelled issuer expectations, not events.
- Nothing dated between November 3, 2026 and the cutoff is supplied. Events in that window are Not supplied, not absent.
### Identity and perimeter

- Reporting entity: Valaris Limited, incorporated in Bermuda, NYSE common shares and warrants (page:1 of each filing); the Q3 release (page:5) calls it "a Bermuda exempted company limited by shares". The context leaves borrower, parent, guarantors and sponsor blank. That is not evidence that none exist.

- Debt issuers: "the Company and Valaris Finance Company LLC" ("Valaris Finance"), a wholly-owned subsidiary, issued the 2030 Second Lien Notes (10-Q Q3 page:21). The notes are guaranteed "by certain subsidiaries of the Company". The revolver is guaranteed by Valaris Finance and certain other subsidiaries (10-Q Q3 page:21; 10-K page:128). The guarantor list itself is not supplied.

- Pending acquirer: Transocean Ltd., a Swiss corporation, under a Business Combination Agreement dated February 9, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:11). Valaris is the target. Transocean's own financial statements are not supplied.

- Unconsolidated affiliate: ARO Drilling, a 50/50 joint venture with Saudi Aramco, equity method (10-K page:122). Valaris holds notes receivable from ARO, leases rigs to ARO and may be asked for capital (10-Q Q3 page:54 to page:56). Operating results of ARO appear in the segment table as a reconciling item, so ARO segment figures are 100 percent of ARO and are not part of consolidated results (Q3 release page:4, footnote 1).
- Currency and units: USD, in millions, in the filings. No other currency is the reporting currency. A Malaysian assessment is stated in MYR with a dollar conversion (10-Q Q3 page:56).
### Consumer evidence demand
| Consumer | Evidence it needs | Located | Limitation carried forward |

| CP-1 | Annual and interim statements, discrete quarters, segments, debt, cash flow, Adjusted EBITDA | 10-K page:105 to page:107, page:127 to page:129; 10-Q Q3 page:8 to page:10, page:21 to page:22, page:51 to page:53; Q3 release page:8 to page:11 | Adjusted EBITDA is a company definition; one debt series, so no facility table beyond the notes and revolver; ARO shown as equity method |

| CP-1A | Business, fleet, customers, transaction, ARO, history | 10-K page:8, page:76; 10-Q Q3 page:11, page:12, page:29 to page:32; Q3 release page:1 to page:3 | Business Combination Agreement, scheme documents and later 8-Ks not supplied; ARO's own statements not supplied |

| CP-2 | CP-1 and CP-1A outputs; liquidity, covenants, commitments, claims outside debt | 10-Q Q3 page:26, page:29, page:51 to page:56; 10-K page:91, page:93, page:128 to page:129 | Covenant levels and ratings not supplied; Notes Receivable from ARO is an asset, not debt |
| CP-5 | Traceable claims | All seven sources have page chunks | Original HTML, charts and tables as filed are not inspected |
### Analytical read-through

- Usable coverage: seven dated filings span the FY2025 audited year and each 2026 quarter. Together they support a reported financial foundation, a last-twelve-months view from the Q3 release's discrete quarters, and a debt and liquidity description of a capital structure that has one note series and one undrawn revolver.

- Strongest contrary evidence: the pending Business Combination (10-Q Q3 page:11 to page:12) can change ownership, covenant treatment and the debt structure. The 10-K (page:127) says that on a "Change of Control Triggering Event" the issuers "may be required to make an offer to repurchase" the notes at "101.0%" of principal. The supplied set does not say whether that event is triggered by the Transocean transaction. It also does not give the combination financing, Transocean's capital structure or the post-closing group.

- Source risk mechanism: the revolver's "financial covenants that require us to maintain (i) a minimum book value of equity to total assets ratio, (ii) a minimum interest coverage ratio and (iii) a minimum amount of liquidity" (10-K page:129) carry no printed level, so a consumer cannot compute headroom and must not infer a pass from the statement that the company is "in compliance in all material respects". Compliance is a management assertion in a filing, not a tested ratio.

- Second mechanism: ARO is outside consolidated debt and earnings. Valaris reports notes receivable from ARO, an investment, lease receivables and payables, a contingent funding commitment for newbuild jackups, and ARO's own revolver and term loan (10-Q Q3 page:54 to page:56). A consumer that reads only consolidated debt omits an exposure that can call on Valaris cash. ARO's statements are not supplied, so the exposure can be described from Valaris's disclosure only.

- Third mechanism: letters of credit and surety bonds sit outside the revolver. The Q3 10-Q (page:26) says none "were issued under the 2028 Credit Agreement". Revolver availability therefore must not be reduced for them without evidence, and must not be assumed unaffected by other conditions on borrowing.

- What cannot proceed: covenant headroom against levels, rating-based pricing, post-closing credit analysis of the combined group, legal interpretation of the indenture and credit agreement, guarantor-level analysis, ARO standalone credit analysis.

- Next evidence action: supply the Business Combination Agreement and any scheme document or proxy, the Indenture dated April 19, 2023 and the 2028 Credit Agreement with covenant definitions, any ratings reports, ARO's financial statements, and any filing dated between November 3, 2026 and the cutoff.
### Debt and liquidity inputs located (no calculation)

- Notes: "$700.0 million" Initial Second Lien Notes (April 2023) and "$400.0 million" Additional Notes (August 2023) form one series, the 2030 Second Lien Notes, 8.375% per annum, maturing April 30, 2030, interest payable April 30 and October 30; issuers the Company and Valaris Finance; secured second lien (10-Q Q3 page:21; 10-K page:127). The 10-K contractual obligations table prints principal due in the "2029 and 2030" column of "1,100.0" and none earlier (10-K page:91).

- Revolver: the 2028 Credit Agreement, commitments of "$375.0 million", maturing April 3, 2028, "$150.0 million sublimit" for letters of credit, "no amounts outstanding" at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:21 to page:22). Availability "$375.0 million" as of October 30, 2026 (page:51).

- Balance sheet: cash and cash equivalents $525.1 million and long-term debt $1,088.5 million at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:9). No separate debt table is printed in the 10-Q; the carrying amount sits on the face of the balance sheet. The 10-K prints a carrying value of the notes, "$1,086.0", and a fair value, "$1,144.9", at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:124).
- Letters of credit and surety bonds: "$113.7 million", none under the revolver (10-Q Q3 page:26).
### Searches made before recording a gap

- Covenant levels: searched all seven sources for "minimum amount of liquidity", "minimum book value", "interest coverage ratio", "leverage ratio" and "maintenance covenant". Only the 10-K names the three tests (page:129, and a risk factor); the three 10-Qs say only that the company was "in compliance in all material respects". No source prints a threshold or a reported ratio. Recorded as Not supplied.

- Ratings: searched for "Moody", "S&P" and "credit rating". Hits are the pricing grid of the revolver and the pension discount rate; no issuer rating is printed. Recorded as Not supplied. The context `ratings` field is empty.

- Letters of credit: searched "letters of credit" and "surety". The Q3 10-Q (page:26 and page:55) prints $113.7 million of letters of credit and surety bonds, none under the revolver. No gap is recorded on this.
- Liquidity inputs: cash and the undrawn revolver are printed (10-Q Q3 page:51); restricted cash is printed separately (page:30). No gap is recorded on the inputs.
## Calculations
No new calculation. CP-0 does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. Coverage counts: seven issuer sources plus the context, no supplied handoffs.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Valaris has one 8.375% second lien note series due 2030 and an undrawn $375.0 million revolver. Leverage on Adjusted EBITDA rose from 1.71 times at FY2025 to 2.68 times on a last-twelve-months basis to Q3 2026. | Medium | Covenant levels, ratings and 2026 cash interest paid are not supplied; Adjusted EBITDA is a company measure. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Adjusted EBITDA fell from 642.2 in FY2025 to 410.8 for the last twelve months to Q3 2026, then recovered to 150.6 in Q3 2026. | Leverage is higher than at FY2025 but the latest quarter is the strongest of the last four. | High |

| Cash was 525.1 at September 30, 2026 against 599.4 at December 31, 2025, with capital expenditure above operating cash flow in 2026. | Free cash flow is negative on a nine-month and last-twelve-months basis, funded from cash. | High |

| Liquidity is cash plus the undrawn $375.0 million revolver, 900.1 at September 30, 2026; no debt principal falls due before 2030. | Near-term refinancing risk is low; the revolver matures in April 2028. | High |
| The revolver carries three financial covenants but no level or reported figure is printed. | Covenant headroom cannot be assessed from these sources. | High |

| The pending Transocean combination and ARO funding commitments sit outside the reported debt figure. | The standalone figures may not describe the post-closing credit; ARO exposure is described only from Valaris disclosure. | Medium |
### Financial base view

The reported statements support a clear standalone financial base. Debt is one instrument: $1,100.0 million of 8.375% Senior Secured Second Lien Notes due April 30, 2030, issued by the Company and Valaris Finance Company LLC, with a carrying value of 1,088.5 at September 30, 2026. The $375.0 million revolver maturing April 3, 2028 has nothing drawn, and none of the letters of credit and surety bonds is issued under it. Cash was 525.1. On those inputs liquidity is 900.1 and net debt (principal less cash) is 574.9.

Earnings fell and then recovered. Issuer-defined Adjusted EBITDA was 642.2 in FY2025, 410.8 for the last twelve months to Q3 2026, and 150.6 in Q3 2026 against 96.5 in Q2 2026. Gross leverage on principal is 1.71 times at FY2025 and 2.68 times on the last-twelve-months basis; net leverage is 0.78 and 1.40 times. Operating cash flow of 155.3 for nine months 2026 did not cover capital expenditure of 328.0, so cash fell and free cash flow was negative. FY2025 net income of 979.1 includes a deferred income tax benefit of 515.1 and is not a measure of cash earnings.

The base is restricted in four ways. First, the covenant levels are not printed, so headroom is Not supplied. Second, cash interest paid is printed only for FY2025, so interest cover on cash interest is available for that year alone. Third, the 2026 figures are standalone while a combination with Transocean is expected to close on or about December 1, 2026. Fourth, ARO is outside consolidated debt and earnings and only Valaris's disclosure of it is supplied. Confidence is High for the reported statement facts and Medium for the credit conclusions that depend on them.

### Source assessment

- 10-K for FY2025 (page:1, signed February 20, 2026; page:163): audited consolidated statements by KPMG LLP (page:104, page:105), USD millions, consolidated Valaris Limited and subsidiaries, US GAAP. Controlling for FY2025 and FY2024 statement facts.

- 10-Qs for Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026: unaudited condensed consolidated statements, same perimeter and currency. The Q3 10-Q (page:11) says "Certain previously reported amounts have been reclassified to conform to the current year presentation."; FY2025 comparatives are taken from the 10-K and Q3 comparatives from the Q3 10-Q.

- Releases: unaudited, management-prepared. The Q3 release repeats the Q3 10-Q statements and adds five discrete quarters, segment Adjusted EBITDA and backlog. Statement figures were matched to the 10-Q where both print them: revenues 555.6, net income 46.7, cash 525.1, operating income 81.3. No conflict found.

- All statement scopes use USD in millions, US GAAP, consolidated Valaris Limited and subsidiaries, with ARO under the equity method. The balance sheet is an instant (September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025); flows carry their own start and end dates.
### Capital structure and debt, all instruments
| Instrument | Issuer and co-issuer | Amount | Rate | Maturity | Security and guarantors | Locator |

| 2030 Second Lien Notes | Valaris Limited and Valaris Finance Company LLC | $700.0 million issued April 2023 at par plus $400.0 million issued August 2023 at 100.75% of par; one series; 1,100.0 principal | 8.375% per annum, payable April 30 and October 30; effective rate 8.76% | April 30, 2030 | Senior secured second priority; guaranteed by "certain subsidiaries of the Company"; secured on a second-priority basis by the Collateral (as defined in the Indenture) | 10-Q Q3 page:21; 10-K page:127 |

| 2028 Credit Agreement (revolver) | Valaris Limited as borrower | Commitments of $375.0 million; accordion of $200.0 million; $150.0 million letter of credit sublimit; nothing drawn | Term SOFR plus 0.10% plus margin of 2.50% to 4.00%, or base rate plus 1.50% to 3.00%; commitment fee 0.375% to 0.75% | April 3, 2028 | First priority; guaranteed by Valaris Finance and certain other subsidiaries; first preferred ship mortgages over collateral vessels | 10-Q Q3 page:21 to page:22; 10-K page:128 to page:129 |

- Series count: the debt note lists the Initial and Additional notes as one series, so there is one note series and one revolver. No other borrowing, term loan or finance lease is listed in the debt note (10-Q Q3 page:21 to page:22).

- Fair value: the notes' estimated fair value is 1,125.2 against carrying value 1,088.5 at September 30, 2026, and 1,144.9 against 1,086.0 at December 31, 2025 (10-Q Q3 page:17; 10-K page:124). Quoted prices are Level 1 inputs per the filing.

- Redemption: from April 30, 2026 the notes are callable at 104.188% falling to 102.094% from April 30, 2027 and par from April 30, 2028 (10-K page:127). The notes carry a change-of-control offer at 101.0% of principal (10-K page:127). Whether the Transocean combination triggers it is not stated in the supplied sources.
- Maturity wall: nothing before 2030 (see the maturities table). Interest on the notes is 92.1 in 2026 and 184.3 for 2027 and 2028 together (10-K page:91).
### Claims outside the debt figure
| Item | Amount | Inside the debt figure? | Locator |
| Lease liabilities (current 27.9, noncurrent 41.3) | 69.2 at September 30, 2026; 72.9 at December 31, 2025 | No | 10-Q Q3 page:29 |
| Pension and other post-retirement benefits | 50.8 at September 30, 2026; 68.3 at December 31, 2025 | No | 10-Q Q3 page:29 |
| Unrecognized tax benefits, with interest and penalties | 136.6 at September 30, 2026 | No | 10-Q Q3 page:29 |

| Letters of credit and surety bonds (including an approximately $75.0 million customs bond) | 113.7; collateral deposits 14.8; none under the revolver | No (off balance sheet contingent) | 10-Q Q3 page:26, page:55 |
| Accrued interest | 38.4 at September 30, 2026; 15.4 at December 31, 2025 | No | 10-Q Q3 page:29 |

| Potential funding of ARO newbuild jackups | Commitment reduced to "$1.1 billion"; maximum aggregate contribution per partner up to $1.25 billion before reductions | No (contingent) | 10-Q Q3 page:56 |
| ARO borrowings: term loan of $359.0 million (8 years, 50% balloon) and revolving facility of up to $150.0 million with $50.0 million outstanding | At ARO, not consolidated | No | 10-Q Q3 page:55 |

- The 10-Q Q3 does not print a Valaris guarantee of ARO borrowings: a search of "guarant" across the 10-Q Q3 and 10-K finds guarantees only of the notes, the revolver and performance instruments. This is a search result, not a legal conclusion.

- Notes Receivable from ARO are an asset: principal 400.7, discount 37.3, carrying 363.4 at September 30, 2026; maturities of 227.3 in October 2027 and 173.4 in October 2028 (10-Q Q3 page:17, page:54). They are subordinated to ARO's term loan and credit facility (page:55). Valaris expects "to agree to extend the maturity" (page:54). Repayment is not assumed here.

- Not supplied: purchase commitments for rigs under construction at Valaris, factoring or supply-chain finance arrangements. A search of the 10-Q Q3 and 10-K for these terms found nothing relevant, so none is recorded and none is assumed to exist.
### Liquidity

- Inputs at September 30, 2026: cash and cash equivalents 525.1 (10-Q Q3 page:9); revolver commitment 375.0 with nothing drawn (page:22); letters of credit and surety bonds issued under the revolver: none (page:26). Restricted cash of 16.5 is excluded (page:30).
- Result: 900.1 (Calculations). The company states it "had $375.0 million available for borrowing" as of October 30, 2026 (page:51).
- The revolver matures April 3, 2028, outside twelve months. Availability is subject to the covenants and conditions of the agreement, which are not supplied.

- After the balance date: the semi-annual coupon is payable October 30, 2026. At 8.375% on 1,100.0 this is a scheduled payment of 46.1 (Calculations). Whether it was paid is not stated in the supplied sources, and no cash balance after September 30, 2026 is supplied.

- Uses of cash in 2026: capital expenditure guidance of $445.0 million to $470.0 million for 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:52), against 328.0 spent in nine months 2026. Merger and integration expenses of 40.5 for nine months (page:12) are cash costs that are not in Adjusted EBITDA.
### Covenants

- Revolver financial covenants: "a minimum book value of equity to total assets ratio, (ii) a minimum interest coverage ratio and (iii) a minimum amount of liquidity" (10-K page:129). Level, step-down, reported figure and headroom: Not supplied. Searches of all seven sources found no threshold or reported ratio.

- Company statement: in compliance "in all material respects" with the Indenture and the 2028 Credit Agreement at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:21, page:22). This is a management statement, not a tested ratio.

- Indenture: incurrence-type limits on debt, liens, restricted payments, asset sales, affiliate transactions and mergers (10-K page:128); many are suspended at investment grade ratings from two agencies. No financial maintenance covenant is described for the notes.
- Definitions: the covenant interest coverage and liquidity definitions are not supplied, so Adjusted EBITDA, interest expense and liquidity as computed here may differ from the covenant definitions.
### Latest quarter and after

- Q3 2026 against Q2 2026 (Q3 release page:2, page:8): revenues exclusive of reimbursables 555.6 against 502.3; Adjusted EBITDA 150.6 against 96.5; net income 46.7 against 47.0. Management attributes the revenue increase to more operating days and higher average daily revenues for the floater fleet, with three drillships starting contracts during the second and third quarters.
- Middle East conflicts reduced Q3 Adjusted EBITDA by approximately $24 million against approximately $30 million in Q2 2026 (release page:2). This is a management estimate.
- Tax expense of 54.7 in Q3 included a discrete tax expense of $23 million, "primarily non-cash" (release page:2).
- Cash fell from 541.2 at June 30, 2026 to 525.1, "primarily due to capital expenditures" partly offset by operating cash flow and asset sale proceeds (release page:2).

- Backlog: 4,750.1 at November 2, 2026 against 4,585.2 at August 5, 2026 and 4,929.1 at May 4, 2026 (release page:11). Backlog is a management measure and may include contracts subject to final investment decision (release page:11, footnote).

- Fleet: VALARIS DS-15 started a contract in September (release page:3); VALARIS DS-18 started after quarter end and VALARIS MS-1 was sold for recycling (release page:1); VALARIS 250 and 116 resumed ARO bareboat charters in July and September (release page:2).

- Transaction: Business Combination Agreement with Transocean Ltd. dated February 9, 2026, exchange ratio of 15.235 Transocean shares per Valaris share; shareholder meetings on November 24, 2026; court hearing on November 26, 2026; expected close on or about December 1, 2026; the release says required regulatory approvals have been received (10-Q Q3 page:11, page:12; release page:1). Dates are expectations, not events. Merger and integration expenses were 15.5 in Q3 and 40.5 for nine months (10-Q Q3 page:12).

- ARO: Kingdom 5 and Kingdom 6 were ordered in August 2026 for about $360.0 million each; ARO's cash was $32.1 million at September 30, 2026 against $99.3 million at December 31, 2025 (10-Q Q3 page:54, page:56; 10-K page:90).
- No filing dated after November 3, 2026 is supplied.
### Segment and operating data
| Q3 2026 against Q2 2026 (US$m) | Floaters | Jackups | ARO (100%) | Other | Reconciling items | Consolidated |
| Revenues exclusive of reimbursable, Q3 2026 | 346.0 | 171.2 | 144.9 | 38.4 | -144.9 | 555.6 |
| Revenues exclusive of reimbursable, Q2 2026 | 279.0 | 183.4 | 126.9 | 39.9 | -126.9 | 502.3 |

Source: Q3 release page:4. Reconciling items include onshore support costs, general and administrative expense and, for Adjusted EBITDA, the removal of ARO. Total fleet utilization was 67% in Q3 2026 and 67% in Q3 2025; average daily revenue was $200,000 against $176,000 (release page:12). The company reports revenue efficiency of 97% for Q3 2026 and 98% year to date (release page:1).
### Definition review and conflicts

- Adjusted EBITDA: the release defines it as "earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, other operating (income) loss, (gain) loss on sale of assets, merger and integration expenses and equity in (earnings) losses of ARO" (release page:11). The recomputation from reported lines reproduces the issuer figures for Q3 2026 (150.6), nine months 2026 (313.8) and FY2025 (642.2); see Calculations. It excludes the equity earnings of ARO and the merger costs, and it is not a covenant measure.

- Conflict, immaterial to the financial base: the Q3 release page:1 describes VALARIS 111 as sold "for conversion to a mobile offshore production unit", while the Q3 10-Q (page:18) says the rig was sold "for recycling" for $1.7 million. Both are quoted and neither is chosen. The 10-Q controls for the accounting; the proceeds are small.

- Correction of an upstream statement: CP-0 cited the FY2025 statement of operations at page:105. The statement runs from page:105 (revenues to depreciation) to page:106 (general and administrative to net income). No figure in CP-0 is affected.

- Prior-period comparability: the 2026 10-Qs state that certain previous amounts were reclassified. No difference between FY2025 totals in the 10-K and the Q4 2025 column plus nine-month 2025 figures was found: FY2025 operating cash flow of 546.2 equals nine months 2025 of 474.0 plus Q4 2025 of 72.2, and capital expenditure of 343.5 equals 237.2 plus 106.3.

Q4 2025 net income of 716.8 carries a benefit of 680.4 (Q3 release page:8). Earnings-based ratios should use Adjusted EBITDA or operating income, not net income.
## Calculations
All inputs are US$m from the cited pages. Results are rounded to one decimal for amounts and two for multiples.

1. Quarterly Adjusted EBITDA (issuer measure, "Valaris Total"): Q1 2025 181.3 (Q1 release page:10); Q2 2025 200.7 (Q2 release page:11); Q3 2025 163.2 and Q4 2025 97.0 (Q3 release page:11); Q1 2026 66.7, Q2 2026 96.5 and Q3 2026 150.6 (Q3 release page:10 to page:11).
5. Recomputation from reported lines, to check the issuer figure (operating income + depreciation + merger and integration expenses + other operating loss (income) - equity in earnings of ARO):
- FY2025: 477.0 + 146.3 + 27.3 - 8.4 = 642.2 (10-K page:105 to page:106). Matches, with the impairment of 27.3 as the other operating loss.

- LTM Q3 2026 from the four quarters of the Q3 release page:8: operating income 39.4 + 20.0 + 51.1 + 81.3 = 191.8; depreciation 40.6 + 42.7 + 44.6 + 47.3 = 175.2; merger costs 0 + 13.6 + 11.4 + 15.5 = 40.5; other operating loss 19.5 - 2.8 + 0 + 3.0 = 19.7; equity in earnings of ARO 2.5 + 6.8 + 10.6 - 3.5 = 16.4. EBITDA = 191.8 + 175.2 + 40.5 + 19.7 - 16.4 = 410.8. Matches.
6. Debt principal: 700.0 + 400.0 = 1,100.0 (10-Q Q3 page:21). No redemption is reported. The 10-K contractual obligations table prints 1,100.0 (page:91).

9. Sensitivity on operating income plus depreciation, which includes the equity result of ARO, merger costs and impairments: LTM Q3 2026 191.8 + 175.2 = 367.0, giving 1,100.0 / 367.0 = 3.00 gross and 574.9 / 367.0 = 1.57 net; FY2025 477.0 + 146.3 = 623.3, giving 1.76 gross and 0.80 net.

10. Interest cover, FY2025: 642.2 / 90.5 = 7.10. Accrual basis: 642.2 / 98.8 = 6.50; LTM Q3 2026 interest expense, net = 24.8 + 24.3 + 24.0 + 24.9 = 98.0 (Q3 release page:8), so 410.8 / 98.0 = 4.19. Against the scheduled 2026 coupon of 92.1 (10-K page:91) cover would be 410.8 / 92.1 = 4.46; this uses a contractual amount and is not interest paid.
11. Scheduled coupon: 1,100.0 x 8.375% / 2 = 46.1 (Indenture terms, 10-Q Q3 page:21). Annual: 92.1, which matches the 10-K contractual interest for 2026.

12. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure: FY2025 546.2 - 343.5 = 202.7; nine months 2026 155.3 - 328.0 = -172.7; Q3 2026 67.2 - 121.6 = -54.4. LTM operating cash flow = 72.2 + 155.3 = 227.5; LTM capital expenditure = 106.3 + 328.0 = 434.3; LTM = 227.5 - 434.3 = -206.8. Q4 2025 values come from the Q3 release page:10 and equal FY2025 less nine months 2025 (546.2 - 474.0 = 72.2; 343.5 - 237.2 = 106.3).

13. Other LTM sums: revenues exclusive of reimbursable 502.2 + 1,488.0 = 1,990.2; total operating revenues 537.4 + 1,598.2 = 2,135.6; interest income 18.7 + 49.6 = 68.3; net income 716.8 + 75.7 = 792.5; asset sale proceeds 1.6 + 102.6 = 104.2; share repurchases 25.0 + 0 = 25.0 (Q4 2025, Q3 release page:10).

### Reader summary

### Business and transaction view

Valaris is a Bermuda-incorporated offshore drilling contractor with a fleet of 41 rigs at September 30, 2026: 13 drillships, 21 jackups and 7 jackups leased to ARO. It earns fixed day rates under contracts that customers can terminate in specified circumstances. The credit case rests on contracted deepwater drillship work with a small number of large customers, and on a capital structure of one note series and an undrawn revolver, described in the financial base view.

The central transaction is the pending acquisition of Valaris by Transocean Ltd. under a Business Combination Agreement dated February 9, 2026. It is a share exchange at 15.235 Transocean shares for each Valaris share, implemented by a Bermuda court-approved scheme of arrangement, and no cash consideration is described. Valaris shareholders would own about 47% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis assuming conversion of Transocean's exchangeable bonds due 2029. Shareholder meetings are set for November 24, 2026, a court hearing for November 26, 2026, and closing is expected on or about December 1, 2026. These are expectations, not completed events. For a creditor the important point is what the sources do not say: no supplied document states whether the combination triggers the change-of-control offer in the Indenture, whether the notes or revolver stay in place, or what the combined capital structure is. Until closing, the agreement restricts dividends, share repurchases, asset encumbrance, acquisitions and dispositions, and new or guaranteed debt.

The business view is otherwise stable to improving on management's account, with specific exposures: customer concentration, termination and FID-contingency rights in contracts, Middle East operations, and ARO funding. The view is Medium confidence. The facts are documentary, but the effect of the combination on creditors is not assessable from the supplied sources.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The one transaction in the sources is the pending business combination with Transocean Ltd., a Swiss corporation. The Business Combination Agreement was entered into on February 9, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:11). Transocean will acquire all issued and outstanding common shares of Valaris in exchange for Transocean shares at an exchange ratio of 15.235 Transocean shares for each Valaris share, by a court-approved scheme of arrangement under section 99 of the Companies Act 1981 of Bermuda (10-K page:8). Outstanding warrants will be assumed by Transocean and remain exercisable for the Fundamental Transaction Consideration as defined in the Warrant Agreement dated April 30, 2021 (10-Q Q3 page:11). On a fully diluted basis assuming conversion of Transocean's exchangeable bonds due 2029, Transocean shareholders would own approximately 53% and Valaris shareholders 47% of the combined company (10-Q Q3 page:11). The type is a stock-for-stock acquisition of Valaris. There is no sponsor, no cash consideration and no use of proceeds in the sources.

Status. Closing is subject to Valaris and Transocean shareholder approvals, a Bermuda sanction order, NYSE listing of the new Transocean shares, regulatory approvals or expiry of waiting periods, no legal prohibition, and the absence of a material adverse effect (10-Q Q3 page:12). Shareholder meetings for both companies are scheduled for November 24, 2026 and the Bermuda sanction hearing for November 26, 2026; closing is expected on or about December 1, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:12; Q3 release page:1). Management states that the combination "has received the required regulatory approvals" (Q3 release page:1). These dates are expectations at the cutoff; no document dated after November 3, 2026 is supplied.

Terms that matter to creditors. A termination fee of $173.0 million is payable by Valaris in specified circumstances; if Valaris shareholders fail to approve and that fee is not otherwise payable, Valaris must reimburse Transocean's transaction expenses up to $58 million (10-K page:22). Either party may terminate if the effective time has not occurred by February 9, 2027, subject to extension (10-K page:22). Valaris is restricted from soliciting alternative proposals and cannot terminate to accept a superior proposal (10-K page:23). Interim covenants restrict amending organizational documents, declaring dividends or repurchasing shares, encumbering assets, acquisitions and dispositions, incurring or guaranteeing indebtedness, and entering or amending material contracts (10-K page:24). Merger and integration expenses were 15.5 in Q3 2026 and 40.5 for nine months 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:12), per the financial base view.

Effect on debt: Not supplied. A search of all seven sources for refinancing, assumption of debt, and the Indenture's change-of-control provision found only the Indenture's 101.0% repurchase offer on a Change of Control Triggering Event (10-K page:127, as set out in the financial base view). No source states whether that event occurs on closing, whether the notes or revolver are repaid, assumed or amended, or what Transocean's own capital structure is. Transocean's financial statements and the Business Combination Agreement itself are not supplied. A creditor therefore cannot size the post-closing leverage, and the standalone figures are the only quantified base.

New debt issues. No new debt was issued in FY2025 or the first nine months of 2026: the cash flow statements show no debt issuance, and the only financing flows are share repurchases in 2025, tax withholdings and a small other item in 2026 (10-K page:107; 10-Q Q3 page:10). The outstanding notes were issued in 2023 and are described in the financial base view. Subsequent events after September 30, 2026 are limited to what the Q3 release and the 10-Q state: the start of the VALARIS DS-18 contract and the shareholder and court dates above.

### ARO and related-party exposure

| Backlog link | ARO backlog (100%) 2,198.6 includes rigs leased from Valaris; Valaris recognizes 50% of ARO earnings as equity income | Documentary Fact | 10-Q Q3 page:35 | ARO earnings are a non-cash equity item that reaches Valaris only through distributions or repayment |
### Differences and conflicts between sources
| Item | Source A | Source B | Treatment |

| Use of VALARIS 111 | Q3 release page:1: sale of "long-term stacked jackup VALARIS 111 for conversion to a mobile offshore production unit" | 10-Q Q3 page:18: "we entered into an agreement to sell VALARIS 111, a rig within our Jackups segment, for recycling for $1.7 million" | Logged, not reconciled. The 10-Q controls the accounting; the amount is small |

| Regulatory approval status | 10-Q Q3 page:12: regulatory approvals "expected to be satisfied by November 3, 2026" | Q3 release page:1: the combination "has received the required regulatory approvals"; 10-Q Q3 page:32: all required approvals obtained and waiting periods "expected to expire or terminate" | Different wording of one status, not a numeric conflict. Logged; confirmation is Not supplied |
| Principal office | 10-K page:1: Clarendon House, 2 Church Street | 10-Q Q3 page:1: Richmond House, 12 Par-la-Ville Road | Change of address between filings, not a conflict of facts |
| Business Combination wording | 10-K page:8 and page:22 | 10-Q Q3 page:11 and page:12 | Consistent on ratio, ownership split and fee; the 10-Q adds the November 24 and 26, 2026 dates |
### Credit translations

- Revenue durability. Evidence: backlog of 4,750.1 at November 2, 2026 against 4,672.3 at February 17, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:35), with contracts that may be terminated for convenience or lack of FID (10-K page:10). Mechanic: contracted day rates give revenue visibility for debt service, but termination rights and the FID contingency make part of the backlog conditional. Implication: contracted revenue supports near-term liquidity while the notes do not mature before 2030; the conditionality argues against treating backlog as committed cash. Counter-evidence: none logged; the backlog by year at November 2, 2026 is Not supplied.

- Margin and cash flow risk. Evidence: drillship average daily revenue rose to $469,000 in Q3 2026 while floater utilization was 58% (Q3 release page:12), and capital expenditure above operating cash flow in 2026 per the financial base view. Mechanic: idle or stacked rigs carry fixed cost, and contract-specific upgrades precede revenue. Implication: improving drillship contracting should lift cash flow, but liquidity depends on those rigs starting work on schedule.

- Concentration. Evidence: five customers at 49% of FY2025 revenues and 11 rigs on national oil company contracts (10-K page:11, page:45). Mechanic: loss or renegotiation of one contract is material, and national oil company terms can be non-negotiable. Implication: tail risk on any single contract; no customer credit assessment is supplied.

- Transaction and creditor control. Evidence: the stock-for-stock combination, the Indenture's change-of-control offer at 101.0%, and the silence of the sources on debt treatment. Mechanic: closing could trigger noteholder rights or change covenant tests, and interim covenants limit new debt until closing. Implication: standalone credit metrics may not describe the issuer after December 1, 2026. This is the key uncertainty.

- ARO. Evidence: notes receivable, newbuild funding commitment, and ARO's thin cash against rising newbuild orders (10-Q Q3 page:54 to page:56). Mechanic: an unconsolidated affiliate can draw on Valaris cash without appearing in debt. Implication: contingent liquidity use; the commitment is a maximum, not an expected call.
- Sponsor alignment. Evidence: no sponsor, no dividends, no repurchases in 2026. Mechanic: no extraction channel is documented. Implication: neutral; behaviour after closing is Not supplied.

## Calculations

No new calculation. Figures are those of the financial base view (CP-1) or are quoted from located sources. The count of 41 Valaris rigs equals the table total in 10-Q Q3 page:28 (13 floaters, 21 jackups, 7 other). The post-closing ownership split of 53% and 47% is quoted, not derived.

| ARO standalone financial statements and its debt documents not supplied; no ARO distribution history beyond the statement that none has been made | Medium | CP-2 | Obtain ARO statements |
| Events between November 3, 2026 and the cutoff not supplied (including shareholder voting outcomes, which fall after the cutoff) | Medium | CP-2 | Obtain later 8-Ks if available |

spans.text: # CP-2 — Fundamental credit synthesis: Valaris Ltd (val)
## Request

Credit synthesis for Valaris Ltd, issuer id `val`, as of 2026-11-05 (cutoff 2026-11-05), pathway `credit_snapshot`, reporting currency USD. Scope is the fundamental credit view built from the financial base view (CP-1) and the business and transaction context (CP-1A) on a standalone basis, with the pending Transocean combination treated as a transaction risk. No peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion is given.
## Sources

The conclusions rest on the upstream handoffs. The source files were used only for the two supplementary checks marked in the calculations. Locators in the evidence trace are `page:N` chunks of the pinned files, not printed pages.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Valaris has low standalone refinancing risk, with liquidity of USD 900.1 million and no debt due before 2030, but earnings fell and spending exceeds cash flow. The pending Transocean takeover could change the credit before the standalone figures are tested. | Medium | Covenant levels, the combination terms and the treatment of the notes are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| Liquidity of USD 900.1 million at September 30, 2026 and no principal due before 2030. | Near-term refinancing and liquidity risk is low on the reported figures. | High |
| Gross leverage rose from 1.71x at FY2025 to 2.68x on a last-twelve-months basis to Q3 2026. | Leverage is moderate but rose as Adjusted EBITDA fell; the latest quarter improved. | High |

| Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD -206.8 million over the last twelve months. | Cash is being used to fund upgrades, so liquidity depends on drillships earning higher day rates. | High |
| The Transocean combination is expected to close on or about December 1, 2026; its effect on the notes is not stated. | Standalone metrics may not describe the issuer after closing. | Medium |
| The revolver has three financial covenants and no level is printed. | Headroom cannot be assessed. | High |
### Credit view

Valaris Ltd has a low standalone refinancing risk and moderate leverage, but its credit quality now depends on a takeover whose effect on creditors is not disclosed. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 900.1 million and no debt principal due before 2030. The weakest point is cash generation: over the last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA of USD 410.8 million was below capital expenditure of USD 434.3 million, and cash fell. Three things decide the outcome: whether idle drillships keep returning to work at higher day rates, how the combination treats the USD 1,100.0 million of notes, and whether ARO draws on Valaris cash. Confidence is Medium.
### Key findings

- Liquidity is the anchor. Valaris held cash of USD 525.1 million and an undrawn USD 375.0 million revolver at September 30, 2026, giving liquidity of USD 900.1 million. The only debt is USD 1,100.0 million of 8.375% second lien notes due April 30, 2030, and the revolver matures April 3, 2028 with nothing drawn. The notes' fair value of USD 1,125.2 million exceeded their principal, which does not point to market stress.

- Earnings fell and then turned. Adjusted EBITDA, the company's own measure, was USD 642.2 million in FY2025 and USD 410.8 million over the last twelve months to Q3 2026, but USD 150.6 million in Q3 2026 against USD 96.5 million in Q2 2026. Gross leverage on principal moved from 1.71x to 2.68x and net leverage from 0.78x to 1.40x. The latest quarter is the strongest of the last four, so the last-twelve-months ratios overstate the current run rate, though the sources give no forecast.

- Spending outruns cash flow. Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of USD 155.3 million did not cover capital expenditure of USD 328.0 million, and the 2026 capital expenditure guidance is USD 445.0 million to USD 470.0 million. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD -206.8 million over the last twelve months. The guidance describes maintenance and upgrade projects including contract-specific work, so part of the spending should earn revenue as rigs start work, but it is funded from cash until then.

- The takeover is the main unknown. Transocean Ltd. will acquire Valaris by share exchange, with closing expected on or about December 1, 2026. The sources do not state whether closing triggers the notes' change-of-control repurchase offer at 101.0%, whether the notes and revolver stay in place, or what the combined capital structure is. Until closing, the agreement restricts new debt, dividends and repurchases.

- Covenant headroom cannot be judged. The revolver carries minimum equity to total assets, minimum interest coverage and minimum liquidity tests with no printed level or reported figure. The company states only that it was in compliance in all material respects.

- ARO is an off-balance-sheet claim on liquidity. Valaris holds notes receivable from ARO with a carrying value of USD 363.4 million that mature in 2027 and 2028 and are subordinated, and it may have to fund ARO newbuilds up to about USD 1.1 billion. ARO had cash of USD 32.1 million and has never paid a distribution.

- Contracted revenue gives visibility but not certainty. Backlog was USD 4,750.1 million at November 2, 2026, concentrated in a few customers, and contracts can be terminated for convenience or if a customer fails to reach a final investment decision.
### Strengths and weaknesses
Strengths.

- Strong liquidity relative to debt service (Documentary Fact; basis: liquidity of USD 900.1 million, cash and revolver figures in the financial base view). Mechanic: cash and an undrawn revolver cover the scheduled interest of about USD 92.1 million a year and 2026 capital spending shortfalls without market access. Implication: low near-term default risk on the standalone figures.

- A short, simple maturity profile (Documentary Fact; basis: debt table and maturities in the financial base view). Mechanic: one note series, no principal before 2030, revolver undrawn. Implication: no principal falls due before 2030, ignoring the combination.

- Contracted revenue visibility (Documentary Fact for backlog; Management Language for the outlook; basis: backlog and operating model rows in the business context). Mechanic: signed day rate contracts and rising drillship day rates support operating cash flow as idle rigs return to work. Implication: supports recovery of earnings, subject to termination rights.

- Restrained shareholder behaviour (Documentary Fact; basis: governance rows). Mechanic: no dividends, no repurchases in 2026, and the combination agreement bars both until closing. Implication: no documented leakage of cash to shareholders.
Weaknesses.

- Negative free cash flow (Documentary Fact; basis: USD -206.8 million last twelve months, USD -172.7 million nine months 2026). Mechanic: upgrade spending is front-loaded against revenue. Implication: cash declined from USD 599.4 million to USD 525.1 million, so the liquidity cushion is being used.

- Earnings trough and idle capacity (Documentary Fact; basis: Adjusted EBITDA and utilization figures). Mechanic: floater utilization of 58% in Q3 2026 means rigs carry cost without revenue. Implication: leverage of 2.68x is above the FY2025 level of 1.71x and sensitive to timing of contract starts.

- Customer concentration and contract terms (Documentary Fact; basis: customer and contract rows). Mechanic: five customers were 49% of FY2025 revenues and some contracts can be ended for convenience. Implication: a single loss would reduce the visibility that supports leverage.

- ARO exposure (Documentary Fact; basis: ARO rows). Mechanic: subordinated notes receivable, newbuild funding commitment and ARO's low cash. Implication: a contingent call on cash outside the debt figure.

- Transaction uncertainty (Insufficient Information on creditor terms; basis: transaction rows). Mechanic: change-of-control terms, covenant tests and capital structure after closing are not supplied. Implication: the standalone view may be superseded; this limits confidence to Medium.

- Covenant and ratings opacity (Insufficient Information; basis: covenant gap). Mechanic: levels, definitions and ratings are not supplied. Implication: availability of the revolver under stress cannot be tested.
### Credit assessment
| Assessment | Category | Confidence | Limitation |

| Moderate standalone credit risk: low near-term liquidity and refinancing risk, moderate and recently higher leverage, negative free cash flow, and a pending takeover with undisclosed creditor terms | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Covenant levels, ratings, the combination agreement and Transocean's capital structure are not supplied; upstream readiness for this module is limited, not full |
### Thesis

Valaris Ltd can service its debt from cash and an undrawn revolver while its drillship fleet returns to work at higher day rates, but the pending Transocean combination and ARO funding obligations mean creditors cannot rely on the standalone figures alone.
Category: Analyst Interpretation. Basis: liquidity, maturity, leverage and cash flow figures in the financial base view; transaction and ARO rows in the business context.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Treatment of the notes and revolver in the Transocean combination | Change-of-control repurchase offer at 101.0% may or may not be triggered; interim covenants limit new debt; combined capital structure is not supplied | Post-closing leverage, security and covenants are unknown; the standalone credit may be replaced | Critical |

| Cash consumption by upgrades while earnings recover | Capital expenditure above operating cash flow in 2026; guidance of USD 445.0 million to USD 470.0 million | Liquidity falls if contract starts slip or day rates fall | Material |

| Covenant headroom unassessable | Three financial covenants on the revolver with no printed level; compliance stated only in general terms | Revolver availability under stress cannot be tested; the revolver is USD 375.0 million of the USD 900.1 million of liquidity | Material |

| ARO funding and note recovery | Newbuild commitment up to about USD 1.1 billion; subordinated notes receivable; ARO cash of USD 32.1 million | A call on Valaris liquidity outside reported debt, or delayed repayment of the notes receivable | Material |

| Customer concentration and termination rights | Top customers hold a large share of revenue; termination for convenience and FID contingency | Backlog of USD 4,750.1 million is less firm than it appears | Material |

| Middle East conflict | Operating income reduced by about USD 62.0 million in nine months 2026 through delays and war-risk insurance | Wider hostilities could raise cost and cause downtime for jackups and ARO | Material |

| Quality of reported equity | Deferred tax assets of USD 1,298.9 million depend on future taxable income | The equity to total assets covenant may be less comfortable than book values suggest if deferred tax assets were impaired | Minor |
### Evidence trace
| Claim | Basis | Locator |
| Liquidity 900.1; cash 525.1; revolver 375.0 undrawn; no principal before 2030 | Financial base view: liquidity chart, maturities chart | 10-Q Q3 page:9, page:22, page:51 |
| Notes fair value 1,125.2 against principal 1,100.0 | Financial base view: capital structure | 10-Q Q3 page:17 |
| Adjusted EBITDA 642.2, 410.8, 150.6 and 96.5; leverage 1.71x, 2.68x, 0.78x, 1.40x | Financial base view: chart data, calculations | Q3 release page:11 |
| Operating cash flow 155.3, capital expenditure 328.0, free cash flow -206.8 | Financial base view: financials table | 10-Q Q3 page:10 |
| Capital expenditure guidance 445.0 to 470.0 | Financial base view: liquidity section | 10-Q Q3 page:52 |
| Combination terms, interim covenants, change-of-control silence | Business context: transaction summary | 10-Q Q3 page:11, page:12; 10-K page:24, page:127 |
| Covenants named, no level | Financial base view: covenants | 10-K page:129 |
| ARO exposure | Business context: ARO table | 10-Q Q3 page:54, page:55, page:56 |
| Customers and termination rights | Business context: operating model | 10-K page:10, page:11 |
| Middle East impact 62.0 | Business context: operating model | 10-Q Q3 page:34 |
| Deferred tax assets 1,298.9; realization depends on future taxable income | Supplementary check against sources, not in upstream figures | 10-Q Q3 page:9; 10-K page:141 |
## Calculations
All inputs are US$m from the upstream handoffs unless marked as a supplementary source check.

1. Q4 2026 cash outlay before operating inflows (indicative, not a forecast). Remaining 2026 capital expenditure from guidance: 445.0 - 328.0 = 117.0 and 470.0 - 328.0 = 142.0. Scheduled October 30, 2026 coupon: 1,100.0 x 8.375% / 2 = 46.1 (from the financial base view). Outlay = 117.0 + 46.1 = 163.1 to 142.0 + 46.1 = 188.1. Cash after these outlays and with no operating cash flow, asset sale proceeds or merger costs: 525.1 - 163.1 = 362.0 to 525.1 - 188.1 = 337.0. Adding the undrawn revolver: 362.0 + 375.0 = 737.0 to 337.0 + 375.0 = 712.0. Q3 2026 operating cash flow was 67.2, which is excluded here. Whether the coupon was paid is not stated in the sources.

2. Adjusted EBITDA less capital expenditure: last twelve months to Q3 2026, 410.8 - 434.3 = -23.5; nine months 2026, 313.8 - 328.0 = -14.2; FY2025, 642.2 - 343.5 = 298.7. Inputs are from the financial base view.

3. Notes fair value over principal at September 30, 2026: 1,125.2 - 1,100.0 = 25.1; 1,125.2 / 1,100.0 = 102.3% of principal. Quoted prices are Level 1 inputs per the filing. The redemption price schedule is 104.188% until April 30, 2027 and 102.094% from then until April 30, 2028 (financial base view).
4. Cash fall: 599.4 - 525.1 = 74.3 from December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026. Over the same nine months operating cash flow was 155.3, capital expenditure 328.0 and asset sale proceeds 102.6.

5. ARO capacity comparison: the maximum funding commitment of about 1.1 billion exceeds liquidity of 900.1 at September 30, 2026. This is a maximum under the Shareholder Agreement, not an expected call.

6. Supplementary source check, equity to total assets (the first covenant named, level Not supplied): total Valaris shareholders' equity 3,271.0 / total assets 5,482.5 = 59.7% at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:9); 3,169.6 / 5,304.8 = 59.7% at December 31, 2025. These are reported book values; the covenant definition may differ. Deferred tax assets 1,298.9 are 23.7% of total assets at September 30, 2026 (1,298.9 / 5,482.5). The 10-K states that realization of substantially all deferred tax assets depends on future taxable income (10-K page:141).
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affected use | Action |

| Treatment of the notes, revolver and change-of-control provision in the Transocean combination not supplied; the business context records the combination agreement as Not supplied | Critical | Post-closing credit view | Obtain the Business Combination Agreement, scheme document and Transocean's filings |
| Covenant levels, definitions and reported figures not supplied | High | Revolver availability, liquidity under stress | Obtain the 2028 Credit Agreement and compliance disclosures |
| Transocean capital structure not supplied | High | Combined credit profile | Obtain Transocean's filings |
| Ratings and market prices not supplied (context empty) | Low | Pricing context; no rating-based view possible | Keep Not supplied |
| Cash interest paid for 2026 not supplied | Medium | Cash interest cover on a last-twelve-months basis | Use accrual basis, labelled, until supplied |
| Cash balance after September 30, 2026, including the October 30, 2026 coupon, not supplied | Medium | Current liquidity | Obtain later filings |
| ARO standalone statements not supplied | Medium | ARO exposure | Obtain ARO statements |
| Backlog by year at November 2, 2026 not supplied | Medium | Revenue visibility | Obtain backlog schedule from the next filing |

| Upstream signals: the business context judged this module READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, not ready, and logs High gaps on the combination documents and Transocean's statements | High | Confidence is held below High | Restated here; resolve through the first two actions above |
| Contract-level terms and customer credit quality not supplied | Medium | Revenue durability | Obtain contract disclosures |
## Next module

- CP-5: trace the claims in the key findings and strengths and weaknesses to the financial base view and the business context. Check that the liquidity, leverage and cash flow figures match the financial base view exactly. Carry the supplementary source check (equity to total assets and deferred tax assets) as a figure that is not in the upstream handoffs.
- Any later committee work: carry the Critical gap on the combination and the covenant gap as restrictions on every conclusion above.

### Evidence trace view

The run is traceable enough for a standalone view of Valaris, and not for the question that matters most, the credit after the Transocean combination closes. Every figure in the financial base view reproduces from the filings, every checked quotation is in the sources, and the business and credit syntheses use only those figures plus two flagged source checks. Of twelve material claims, six are directly sourced, three are calculated, one is analyst inference and two are Insufficient Information. The critical provenance gap is the Business Combination Agreement: no supplied source says what happens to the notes or the revolver, and the credit synthesis rests its Critical risk and Medium confidence on that silence. Remediation owner: the sourcing step. Five minor defects need no change to any conclusion.
